newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NTT, BT group could spend S$1b in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: NTT, BT group could spend S$1b in Singapore.

text.p: Nippon Telephone and Telegraph Corp (NTT), British Telecommunications Plc, Singapore Power (SP) and Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT) could spend Singapore $1 to S$1.5 billion if they win a licence to provide telephone service in Singapore, an STT executive said.

Asked about possible infrastructure investments in Singapore if the licence was won, STT President Lee Theng Kiat told Reuters on Tuesday: "There are people who say the investment amount would be S$1 billion to S$1.5 billion. I would say that figure is close."
He added that it could be more.
Lee was speaking after a news conference launching a new multi-media forum of Asian telecommunications carriers.
He said the investment in infrastructure would begin in the middle of 1998 if the licence was granted.
The group including BT and NTT and state-owned STT and SP is one of three consortiums competing for the one or two full telecommunications licences Singapore has said it would award next year.
The licences would permit them to compete with current monopoly telephone service provider Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
